title: The map: our city from above
note: Direction A as the user picked it: an aerial render of our own city in lit tiles with smooth zoom, fog over ground you haven't walked, the route in amber, our own blip drawings with no discs, landmark silhouettes, and street and district names placed so nothing collides. Legend, tools and the data credit live in one slim panel.
ref: GTA V/VI render the world from above and mute it so blips read; RDR2 fogs what you haven't seen. We do both. Short of GTA: no zoomed-out regional view yet (the playable sheet is the whole world).

title: Map: a selected story place
note: The card sits at the top of the panel, never over the map: an amber label, the name in Franklin, the time window as a quiet amber line, one primary action.

title: HUD in play
note: Type on the world, not plates: the objective set in Franklin under an amber rule, clock and cash top right, the place you enter wiped in big over an amber bar. The minimap is a square window onto the same aerial. Routine discoveries are silent.
ref: GTA V/VI: radar bottom-left, minimal text. RDR2: meters that fade. Ours fades by setting; heat is radio text and cones, not stars.

title: Mission end: done
note: A band wiped across the frame, the mission's name huge, the cut counting up in money green. Original wording and layout.
ref: GTA's pass screen is a centred banner; ours is a left-weighted band so the world stays in frame.

title: Mission end: failed
note: Same band, a red rule, one plain line for why.

title: Pockets
note: The hub header is the system: the screen name huge, where and when under it, icon tabs, money right. Pockets is one list grouped by where things sit on you (hidden, bulging, seen), and one hero: your cash, or the item you pick.
ref: RDR2's satchel is a grid of items; ours keeps concealment as the organising idea, which is this game's rule.

title: Paper
note: The newspaper is the object and the hero, straight on, print-correct. The UI rail beside it switches pages and counts the ads you can add to your map.
ref: RDR2's newspaper is the closest reference; ours is playable (ads add places, results feed the numbers).

title: Paper: results and the number
note: The runner's betting slip moved out of the paper into the UI rail: three digit wheels and the stakes.

title: Business
note: This week's take as the hero number over an eight-week band; trouble first, as actions; then the book as a ledger.
ref: GTA V's property management is a list; ours leads with the number and the problems.

title: Cars
note: The car that needs you is the hero: a New York plate, the car drawn in its paint, the boot, and the summonses as paper stubs with their own Pay buttons.
ref: Short of GTA: drawn car profiles stand in for renders of the actual car.

title: Used-car lot: haggling
note: Played as a sales scene: the salesman's line in big type, asking against his counter against your offer in big numbers, the stepper, the lot as a list.

title: The fence
note: Dense rows (carry slot, illegal tag, price, what you're short); the keeper's line and your cash beside them.

title: Switch to…
note: No fake portraits: three strips with each lead's colour, name, where they are and their cash; the chosen one widens.
ref: GTA V's switch wheel uses portraits; ours waits for character renders and lets the type carry it.

title: Weapon selector
note: A hairline ellipse over the live street, square nodes, concealment as coloured marks. The HUD steps back while it's open.

title: Dialogue choices
note: One left-of-centre list with number keys, lines set in Franklin; untimed unless the scene says so.

title: Wait until
note: A band whose hero is the time; the job on the left, the decision on the right.

title: Sleep
note: Wake-up times as a column of big times, an hour stepper, rest quality beside it.

title: Parking summons
note: Diegetic paper: a pink summons copy with typed fields, set right of centre; one small UI strip under it.

title: Home upgrades
note: The super's estimate as a typed work order you pick from; his line and your cash beside it.

title: Settings
note: A section rail beside one group at a time, a big heading, dense ruled rows; unwired options say when they'll apply.
ref: GTA V/RDR2 settings are long lists; ours groups them and says what isn't live yet.

title: Buttons and keys
note: A remap table with square keycaps.

title: Saves
note: The profile you're playing is the hero; slots as dense ruled rows.

title: Title
note: Our wordmark over the live city; Continue is the biggest item and says where you left off.

title: Loading
note: A big percentage over an amber bar, over the city as it streams in.
